bills.title: Budget 2026 Implementation Act, No. 1
bills.long: An Act to implement certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on November 5, 2026
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Title only: implements certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on November 5, 2026. No official summary is available, so specific measures cannot be confirmed.

bills.title: Grocery and Housing Affordability Act
bills.long: An Act respecting certain measures related to affordability and housing
bills.sponsor: Gregor Robertson (Liberal MP for Vancouver Fraserview—South Burnaby)
bills.status: At second reading in the Senate
bills.note: Grocery and Housing Affordability Act. No official summary is available, so the title alone indicates measures on affordability and housing.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Competition Act (automated personalized pricing)
bills.long: An Act to amend the Competition Act (automated personalized pricing)
bills.sponsor: Jenny Kwan (NDP MP for Vancouver East)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would make using automated decision-making systems and consumer data to set or adjust individual consumers' prices reviewable conduct under the Competition Act.

bills.title: Canadian Prosperity Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Competition Act
bills.status: Senate bill awaiting first reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would let the Competition Commissioner recommend that governments remove internal trade barriers that unduly harm competition, requiring federal responses within 120 days and publication of responses.

bills.title: Medical Assistance in Dying Safeguards Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Criminal Code and An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying) and to make related amendments to other Acts
bills.sponsor: Sean Fraser (Liberal MP for Central Nova)
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would allow advance requests for medical assistance in dying to be honoured when a person loses capacity, if eligibility, safeguards and provincial repository rules are met, and keep the mental illness exclusion.

bills.title: Cities and Municipalities Day Act
bills.long: An Act respecting a Cities and Municipalities Day
bills.status: Senate bill awaiting first reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Designates October 31 as Cities and Municipalities Day. It is a symbolic designation with no stated operative provisions.

bills.title: National Framework on Skilled Trades and Labour Mobility Act
bills.long: An Act to establish a national framework respecting skilled trades and labour mobility
bills.sponsor: Parm Bains (Liberal MP for Richmond East—Steveston)
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the House of Commons
bills.note: Provides for a national framework to recognize skilled trades, harmonize credential recognition, and improve mobility of skilled trades workers across Canada.

bills.title: An Act to authorize certain payments to be made out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the purpose of improving housing supply
bills.sponsor: François-Philippe Champagne (Liberal MP for Saint-Maurice—Champlain)
bills.status: Royal assent received
bills.note: Authorizes payments from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to provinces and territories to improve housing supply.

bills.title: Stopping Supply to Save Lives Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and to make a related amendment to the Criminal Code
bills.sponsor: Chak Au (Conservative MP for Richmond Centre—Marpole)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would raise penalties for trafficking, importing, exporting or producing large amounts of synthetic opioids, add aggravating factors, and make certain offenders ineligible for parole for 25 years.

bills.title: Housing Cost Transparency Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the National Research Council Act
bills.sponsor: Brad Redekopp (Conservative MP for Saskatoon West)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Amends the National Research Council Act so the NRC publishes standardized housing cost summaries, governance transparency information, and a public registry for housing-related model code proposals.

bills.title: An act to amend the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and the Food and Drugs Act
bills.long: An act to amend the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and the Food and Drugs Act
bills.sponsor: Corey Tochor (Conservative MP for Saskatoon East)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would allow psilocin and psilocybin to be used for medical treatment under the Narcotic Control Regulations, and provide automatic approval of requests for priority review of certain new drugs.

bills.title: An Act to enact the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act, to amend the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act and to make amendments to other Acts
bills.sponsor: Evan Solomon (Liberal MP for Toronto Centre)
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would enact the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act to govern personal information in commercial activities, repeal Part 1 of PIPEDA, and rename that Act the Electronic Documents Act.

bills.title: Bail and Sentencing Reform Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Criminal Code, the Youth Criminal Justice Act and the National Defence Act (bail and sentencing)
bills.sponsor: Sean Fraser (Liberal MP for Central Nova)
bills.status: Royal assent received
bills.note: Amends the Criminal Code and related Acts on bail and sentencing, including reverse onus for certain violent, weapons and motor vehicle theft offences and conditions for release.

bills.title: Used Car Tax Cut Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Excise Tax Act (used motor vehicles)
bills.sponsor: Andrew Lawton (Conservative MP for Elgin—St. Thomas—London South)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would add used motor vehicles to the list of zero-rated supplies under the Excise Tax Act.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Food and Drugs Act (List of Therapeutic Products Pre-approved for Special Access)
bills.sponsor: Marcus Powlowski (Liberal MP for Thunder Bay—Rainy River)
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would amend the Food and Drugs Act to create a list of therapeutic products pre-approved for special access, streamlining treatment for patients with serious or life-threatening conditions or unmet needs. It would also guide the Minister in issuing emergency treatment authorization letters.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Energy Efficiency Act
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Amends the Energy Efficiency Act to allow regulatory exemptions, add administrative monetary penalties and corrective orders, and cover new technologies and market actors.

bills.title: Mental Health Parity Act
bills.long: An Act to enact the Mental Health, Addictions and Substance Use Services Act and to make consequential amendments to the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act
bills.sponsor: Gord Johns (NDP MP for Courtenay—Alberni)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would enact the Mental Health Parity Act, setting criteria that mental health, addictions and substance use services must meet before federal cash contributions to provinces. It also makes consequential amendments to the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act.

bills.title: Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 2
bills.long: A second Act to implement certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on November 4, 2025
bills.sponsor: François-Philippe Champagne (Liberal MP for Saint-Maurice—Champlain)
bills.status: At third reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: A second act implementing certain provisions of the budget tabled November 4, 2025. No official summary is available, so its specific contents cannot be described.

bills.title: Offender Rehabilitation Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Criminal Code, to make related amendments to the Corrections and Conditional Release Act and to amend the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act
bills.sponsor: Kelly DeRidder (Conservative MP for Kitchener Centre)
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would let courts order offenders to complete measures such as treatment or training during custody, and require parole assessments to consider progress. It also treats large-scale fentanyl trafficking as an aggravating factor at sentencing.

bills.title: Connected Care for Canadians Act
bills.long: An Act respecting the interoperability of health information technology and to prohibit data blocking by health information technology vendors
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would require health information technology vendors to ensure interoperability and prohibit data blocking, to promote a connected, secure, person-centered health system.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Criminal Code (assault against persons who provide health services and first responders)
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would require courts to treat assault against health service providers and first responders as an aggravating circumstance at sentencing.

bills.title: National Framework for Women’s Health in Canada Act
bills.long: An Act to establish a national framework for women’s health in Canada
bills.status: At consideration in committee in the Senate
bills.note: Would provide for the development of a national framework to promote, enhance and protect women's health as a matter of national concern.

bills.title: Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1
bills.long: An Act to implement certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on November 4, 2025
bills.sponsor: François-Philippe Champagne (Liberal MP for Saint-Maurice—Champlain)
bills.status: Royal assent received
bills.note: Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 would implement certain provisions of the budget tabled November 4, 2025. No official summary is available, so its specific measures are unknown.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (supervised drug consumption sites)
bills.sponsor: Dan Mazier (Conservative MP for Riding Mountain)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would bar regulations and exemptions under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act from allowing supervised drug consumption sites within 500 metres of schools, daycares, or playgrounds.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Food and Drugs Act (natural health products)
bills.sponsor: Blaine Calkins (Conservative MP for Ponoka—Didsbury)
bills.status: At report stage in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would declare natural health products not therapeutic products under the Food and Drugs Act, so they would not be subject to the same monitoring regime as other drugs.

bills.title: National Strategy on Housing for Young Canadians Act
bills.long: An Act to establish a national strategy on housing for young Canadians
bills.sponsor: Braedon Clark (Liberal MP for Sackville—Bedford—Preston)
bills.status: At report stage in the House of Commons
bills.note: Provides for a national strategy on housing for young Canadians to improve access to affordable and secure housing, with reporting requirements.

bills.title: Preventing Coercion of Persons Not Seeking Medical Assistance in Dying Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying — protection against coercion)
bills.sponsor: Garnett Genuis (Conservative MP for Sherwood Park—Fort Saskatchewan)
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons

bills.title: An Act to amend the Customs Act and the Customs Tariff (forced labour and child labour)
bills.sponsor: Simon-Pierre Savard-Tremblay
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would require customs officers to detain goods until satisfied they are not prohibited, and create a presumption that goods from certain areas or entities involve forced or child labour.

bills.title: Jail Not Bail Act
bills.long: An Act to amend the Criminal Code and the Department of Justice Act
bills.sponsor: Arpan Khanna (Conservative MP for Oxford)
bills.status: Bill defeated
bills.note: Amends the Criminal Code to make public protection a key factor in bail, expands reverse-onus offences, restricts releases and sureties, and requires passport deposits for non-citizens.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Canada Health Act (accountability)
bills.sponsor: Sukh Dhaliwal (Liberal MP for Surrey Newton)
bills.status: At second reading in the House of Commons
bills.note: Would require provinces to implement an accountability framework for health service delivery to receive a full cash contribution under the Canada Health Transfer.

bills.title: One Canadian Economy Act
bills.long: An Act to enact the Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act and the Building Canada Act
bills.sponsor: Dominic LeBlanc (Liberal MP for Beauséjour)
bills.status: Royal assent received
bills.note: One Canadian Economy Act would enact the Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act and the Building Canada Act. No official summary is available, so other provisions are unknown.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying)
bills.sponsor: Tamara Jansen (Conservative MP for Cloverdale—Langley City)
bills.status: Bill defeated
bills.note: Would provide that a mental disorder is not a grievous and irremediable medical condition for which a person could receive medical assistance in dying.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Food and Drugs Act (warning label on alcoholic beverages)
bills.status: Bill defeated
bills.note: Would amend the Food and Drugs Act to require a warning label on alcoholic beverages.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying)
bills.status: At second reading in the Senate
bills.note: Would allow advance written MAID arrangements for a specified day if a person loses capacity beforehand, and written declarations waiving final consent for people with serious, incurable illness who lose capacity.

bills.title: An Act to amend the National Housing Strategy Act
bills.sponsor: Jenny Kwan (NDP MP for Vancouver East)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Requires the National Housing Strategy to prevent removal of homeless encampments on federal land and identify alternatives, with Indigenous involvement and expanded triennial reporting.

bills.title: An Act to amend the Canada Health Act (mental, addictions and substance use health services)
bills.sponsor: Gord Johns (NDP MP for Courtenay—Alberni)
bills.status: Outside the Order of Precedence
bills.note: Would add mental, addictions and substance use health services to the Canada Health Act's definition of insured health services.

b:C-297.summary: This enactment amends the Competition Act to provide that the use of automated decision-making systems and consumer data to determine or adjust the price of goods or services offered to an individual consumer constitutes reviewable conduct under Part VII.‍1 of that Act.
b:C-297.sponsor: Jenny Kwan (NDP MP for Vancouver East)
b:C-297.note: Would make using automated decision-making systems and consumer data to set or adjust individual consumers' prices reviewable conduct under the Competition Act.

b:S-239.summary: This enactment amends section 10.‍1 of the Competition Act to provide that the Commissioner of Competition may, in a market or industry inquiry report, make recommendations to a responsible federal or provincial institution respecting barriers to trade within Canada that, in the Commissioner’s opinion, unduly affect the state of competition in the market or industry. It provides that the head of a federal institution must respond to any recommendation made to the institution within 120 days. It requires the Commissioner to publish the response received on a publicly available website. It provides that the head of a provincial institution may respond to any recommendation made to the institution within 120 days. It requires the Commissioner to publish the response — or, if no response is received, a notice to this effect — on a publicly available website. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-239 An Act to amend the Competition Act
b:S-239.note: Would let the Competition Commissioner recommend that governments remove internal trade barriers that unduly harm competition, requiring federal responses within 120 days and publication of responses.

b:C-41.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to, among other things, (a) clarify that a person cannot receive medical assistance in dying on the basis of a mental illness; and (b) create exemptions from the offences of culpable homicide and administering a noxious thing, in order to permit a medical practitioner or a nurse practitioner to provide medical assistance in dying to a person who has lost the capacity to consent to the procedure if the person made an advance request to receive medical assistance in dying when they had that capacity and if (i) the person is eligible to receive medical assistance in dying and the medical practitioner or nurse practitioner ensures that the applicable safeguards are complied with, (ii) the person prepared their advance request in accordance with the applicable criteria, including that the person was diagnosed, before the request was signed, with a serious and incurable illness or disease that was reasonably expected to lead to an irreversible loss of the capacity to consent to receiving medical assistance in dying, and (iii) the province in which the person would receive medical assistance in dying has in force a provincial legislative regime that identifies the repository in which advance requests are stored and that includes rules in relation to, among other things, making, storing, withdrawing and amending or replacing advance requests. The enactment also amends An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying) so that the exclusion from eligibility to receive medical assistance in dying in relation to a mental illness remains in force. Finally, the enactment makes related amendments to other Acts.
b:C-41.sponsor: Sean Fraser (Liberal MP for Central Nova)
b:C-41.note: Would allow advance requests for medical assistance in dying to be honoured when a person loses capacity, if eligibility, safeguards and provincial repository rules are met, and keep the mental illness exclusion.

b:C-38.summary: This enactment amends the Excise Tax Act to extend the temporary suspension of the federal fuel excise tax until January 31, 2027 and to temporarily set the excise tax rates on fuels to 50% of the regular rates for the period beginning on February 1, 2027 and ending on March 31, 2027.
b:C-38.note: Would extend the federal fuel excise tax suspension to January 31, 2027, and set fuel excise rates at 50% of regular rates from February 1 to March 31, 2027.

b:C-289.summary: This enactment amends the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act to increase penalties for offenders who traffic, possess for the purpose of trafficking, import, export or produce certain amounts of synthetic opioids. It also amends that Act to add as aggravating factors for sentencing purposes in relation to offences respecting synthetic opioids the fact that the offence was committed in proximity to certain facilities or that the offence involved a certain amount of the substance. Finally, it amends the Criminal Code to provide that certain offenders who traffic, possess for the purpose of trafficking, import, export or produce certain amounts of synthetic opioids are ineligible for parole for 25 years.
b:C-289.sponsor: Chak Au (Conservative MP for Richmond Centre—Marpole)
b:C-289.note: Would raise penalties for trafficking, importing, exporting or producing large amounts of synthetic opioids, add aggravating factors, and make certain offenders ineligible for parole for 25 years.

b:C-286.summary: This enactment amends the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and the Food and Drugs Act to allow psilocin and psilocybin to be used for medical treatment in accordance with the Narcotic Control Regulations . It also provides for the automatic approval of requests for priority review for certain new drugs.
b:C-286.sponsor: Corey Tochor (Conservative MP for Saskatoon East)
b:C-286.note: Would allow psilocin and psilocybin to be used for medical treatment under the Narcotic Control Regulations, and provide automatic approval of requests for priority review of certain new drugs.

b:C-36.summary: This enactment enacts the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act to govern the protection of personal information of individuals while taking into account the need of organizations to collect, use or disclose personal information in the course of commercial activities. Consequently, it repeals Part 1 of the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act and changes the short title of that Act to the Electronic Documents Act . Finally, it also makes amendments to other Acts.
b:C-36.sponsor: Evan Solomon (Liberal MP for Toronto Centre)
b:C-36.note: Would enact the Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act to govern personal information in commercial activities, repeal Part 1 of PIPEDA, and rename that Act the Electronic Documents Act.

b:C-285.summary: This enactment amends the Excise Tax Act in order to add used motor vehicles to the list of zero-rated supplies.
b:C-285.sponsor: Andrew Lawton (Conservative MP for Elgin—St. Thomas—London South)
b:C-285.note: Would add used motor vehicles to the list of zero-rated supplies under the Excise Tax Act.

b:C-265.summary: This enactment amends the Food and Drugs Act to establish a list of therapeutic products pre-approved for special access to allow streamlined access to treatment for patients with serious or life-threatening conditions or where there is an unmet need. It also provides parameters to guide the Minister of Health in issuing letters of authorization for the sale of new drugs for emergency treatment under the Food and Drug Regulations .
b:C-265.sponsor: Marcus Powlowski (Liberal MP for Thunder Bay—Rainy River)
b:C-265.note: Would amend the Food and Drugs Act to create a list of therapeutic products pre-approved for special access, streamlining treatment for patients with serious or life-threatening conditions or unmet needs. It would also guide the Minister in issuing emergency treatment authorization letters.

b:C-280.summary: This enactment enacts the Mental Health Parity Act , which sets out criteria and conditions in respect of mental health, addictions and substance use services that must be satisfied before a cash contribution may be made by the Government of Canada to a province in support of those services. It also makes consequential amendments to the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act .
b:C-280.note: Would enact the Mental Health Parity Act, setting criteria that mental health, addictions and substance use services must meet before federal cash contributions to provinces. It also makes consequential amendments to the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act.

b:C-240.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to provide that a court may, by order, in addition to any term of imprisonment imposed on an offender for the commission of an offence, prescribe measures that the offender is to take during the custodial period of their sentence, which may include participation in educational, training or treatment programs. It also makes related amendments to the Corrections and Conditional Release Act to, among other things, provide that objectives with regard to programs that the offender may be required to complete during the custodial period of their sentence are to be included in the correctional plan developed by the head of the facility in which the offender is held and to provide that the assessments that parole boards take into consideration when making a determination regarding the granting of parole are to include information on the progress made by an offender with regard to any prescribed measures that the offender was required to take. Finally, the enactment amends the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act to provide that a court imposing a sentence on a person convicted of trafficking in fentanyl must consider as an aggravating factor the fact that the person trafficked it in quantities that indicate trafficking on a large scale.
b:C-240.sponsor: Kelly DeRidder (Conservative MP for Kitchener Centre)
b:C-240.note: Would let courts order offenders to complete measures such as treatment or training during custody, and require parole assessments to consider progress. It also treats large-scale fentanyl trafficking as an aggravating factor at sentencing.

b:S-5.summary: This enactment aims, among other things, to ensure that health information technology that is licensed, sold or supplied as a service by a vendor is interoperable and to prohibit data blocking by the vendor in order to promote a connected, secure and person-centered health system. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 - 2026 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-5 An Act respecting the interoperability of health information technology and to prohibit data blocking by health information technology vendors
b:S-5.note: Would require health information technology vendors to ensure interoperability and prohibit data blocking, to promote a connected, secure, person-centered health system.

b:S-233.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to require a court to consider the fact that the victim of an assault is a person who provides health services or a first responder to be an aggravating circumstance for the purposes of sentencing. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-233 An Act to amend the Criminal Code (assault against persons who provide health services and first responders)
b:S-233.note: Would require courts to treat assault against health service providers and first responders as an aggravating circumstance at sentencing.

b:C-31.note: A second act implementing certain provisions of the budget tabled November 4, 2025. No official summary is available, so its specific contents cannot be described.

b:C-273.summary: This enactment amends the Feeds Act , the Fertilizers Act , the Seeds Act and the Pest Control Products Act to provide for provisional registration or approval of feeds, fertilizers, seeds and pest control products that are already approved by two or more trusted jurisdictions. It also amends the Food and Drugs Act to provide that the Minister may, by order, deem that specified requirements of that Act or the regulations are met in respect of a veterinary drug on the basis of a decision of, or any information or document produced by, a foreign regulatory authority.
b:C-273.sponsor: David Bexte (Conservative MP for Bow River)
b:C-273.note: Would allow provisional registration of feeds, fertilizers, seeds and pest control products already approved by two or more trusted jurisdictions. It would also let the Minister deem Food and Drugs Act requirements met for veterinary drugs based on foreign regulator decisions.

b:S-243.summary: This enactment provides for the development of a national framework to promote, enhance and protect women’s health as a matter of national concern. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-243 An Act to establish a national framework for women’s health in Canada
b:S-243.note: Would provide for the development of a national framework to promote, enhance and protect women's health as a matter of national concern.

b:C-15.note: Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 would implement certain provisions of the budget tabled November 4, 2025. No official summary is available, so its specific measures are unknown.

b:C-272.summary: This enactment amends the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act to provide that regulations made and exemptions granted under that Act must not have the effect of allowing a site providing services in relation to the consumption of certain substances to be located within 500 metres of an elementary or secondary school, a daycare centre or a playground.
b:C-272.sponsor: Dan Mazier (Conservative MP for Riding Mountain)
b:C-272.note: Would bar regulations and exemptions under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act from allowing supervised drug consumption sites within 500 metres of schools, daycares, or playgrounds.

b:C-224.summary: This enactment amends the Food and Drugs Act to provide that natural health products are not therapeutic products within the meaning of that Act and, therefore, are not subject to the same monitoring regime as other drugs.
b:C-224.note: Would declare natural health products not therapeutic products under the Food and Drugs Act, so they would not be subject to the same monitoring regime as other drugs.

b:C-260.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to make it an offence for certain persons in certain circumstances to initiate a discussion with a person about the availability to them of medical assistance in dying, knowing that they have not specifically requested to have such a discussion.
b:C-260.sponsor: Garnett Genuis (Conservative MP for Sherwood Park—Fort Saskatchewan)
b:C-260.note: Would make it an offence in certain circumstances to initiate discussion of medical assistance in dying with a person who has not specifically requested it.

b:C-251.summary: This enactment amends the Customs Act to require customs officers to detain certain goods until they are satisfied that the goods are not goods the importation of which is prohibited. It also amends the Customs Tariff to establish a presumption that goods from certain areas or entities were mined, manufactured or produced wholly or in part by forced labour or child labour.
b:C-251.note: Would require customs officers to detain goods until satisfied they are not prohibited, and create a presumption that goods from certain areas or entities involve forced or child labour.

b:C-239.summary: This enactment amends the Canada Health Act to require provinces to implement an accountability framework in relation to the delivery of health services in order to qualify for a full cash contribution as part of the Canada Health Transfer.
b:C-239.sponsor: Sukh Dhaliwal (Liberal MP for Surrey Newton)
b:C-239.note: Would require provinces to implement an accountability framework for health service delivery to receive a full cash contribution under the Canada Health Transfer.

b:C-5.note: One Canadian Economy Act would enact the Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act and the Building Canada Act. No official summary is available, so other provisions are unknown.

b:C-218.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to provide that a mental disorder is not a grievous and irremediable medical condition for which a person could receive medical assistance in dying.
b:C-218.sponsor: Tamara Jansen (Conservative MP for Cloverdale—Langley City)
b:C-218.note: Would provide that a mental disorder is not a grievous and irremediable medical condition for which a person could receive medical assistance in dying.

b:C-217.summary: This enactment provides for financial assistance for Canadians with disabilities to improve their access to post-secondary education.
b:C-217.sponsor: Don Davies (NDP MP for Vancouver Kingsway)
b:C-217.note: Would provide financial assistance for Canadians with disabilities to improve their access to post-secondary education.

b:S-202.summary: This enactment amends the Food and Drugs Act to require a warning label on alcoholic beverages. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-202 An Act to amend the Food and Drugs Act (warning label on alcoholic beverages)
b:S-202.note: Would amend the Food and Drugs Act to require a warning label on alcoholic beverages.

b:S-231.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to (a) permit an individual whose death is not reasonably foreseeable to enter into a written arrangement to receive medical assistance in dying on a specified day if they lose the capacity to consent to receiving medical assistance in dying prior to that day; and (b) permit an individual who has been diagnosed with a serious and incurable illness, disease or disability to make a written declaration to waive the requirement for final consent when receiving medical assistance in dying if they lose the capacity to consent to receive medical assistance in dying, are suffering from symptoms outlined in the written declaration and have met all other relevant safeguards outlined in the Criminal Code . Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-231 An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying)
b:S-231.note: Would allow advance written MAID arrangements for a specified day if a person loses capacity beforehand, and written declarations waiving final consent for people with serious, incurable illness who lose capacity.

b:C-201.summary: This enactment amends the Canada Health Act to add mental, addictions and substance use health services to the definition of “insured health services”.
b:C-201.note: Would add mental, addictions and substance use health services to the Canada Health Act's definition of insured health services.

b:C-43.note: Title only: implements certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on November 5, 2026. No official summary is available, so specific measures cannot be confirmed.

b:C-42.note: Grocery and Housing Affordability Act. No official summary is available, so the title alone indicates measures on affordability and housing.

b:S-237.summary: This enactment designates the 31st day of October as “Cities and Municipalities Day”. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-237 An Act respecting a Cities and Municipalities Day
b:S-237.note: Designates October 31 as Cities and Municipalities Day. It is a symbolic designation with no stated operative provisions.

b:C-266.summary: This enactment provides for the development of a national framework for the recognition of skilled trades, harmonization of credential recognition and mobility of skilled trades workers in Canada.
b:C-266.sponsor: Parm Bains (Liberal MP for Richmond East—Steveston)
b:C-266.note: Provides for a national framework to recognize skilled trades, harmonize credential recognition, and improve mobility of skilled trades workers across Canada.

b:C-26.summary: This enactment authorizes payments to be made out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund to the provinces and territories for the purpose of improving housing supply.
b:C-26.note: Authorizes payments from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to provinces and territories to improve housing supply.

b:C-287.summary: This enactment amends the National Research Council Act to provide that, in its role supporting the national model code development system, the National Research Council must prepare, maintain and publish the following: (a) standardized housing cost and impact summaries for material housing-related model code proposals to be used in the public review of those proposals; (b) governance transparency information respecting such proposals, including relevant committee memberships, roles and institutional or organizational affiliations; and (c) an accessible public registry of such proposals and associated materials that includes edition-level and annual summaries of code development activities and impacts.
b:C-287.sponsor: Brad Redekopp (Conservative MP for Saskatoon West)
b:C-287.note: Amends the National Research Council Act so the NRC publishes standardized housing cost summaries, governance transparency information, and a public registry for housing-related model code proposals.

b:C-14.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code to, among other things, (a) provide direction to peace officers, justices and judges when they apply the principle of restraint; (b) require a justice, before making a release order or a detention order in respect of an accused, to consider whether the accused is charged with an offence in the commission of which random and unprovoked violence was used or attempted; (c) require a justice to impose a condition prohibiting the possession of a firearm or other weapon, and to consider imposing other conditions, when making a release order in respect of an accused charged with the offence of extortion or any offence involving a criminal organization; (d) require a justice to consider imposing certain conditions when making a release order in respect of an accused charged with an offence of motor vehicle theft or with the offence of breaking and entering a dwelling-house; (e) create a reverse onus provision for any accused charged with the offence of motor vehicle theft involving violence, motor vehicle theft for a criminal organization, extortion involving violence, breaking and entering a dwelling-house, certain offences related to trafficking in persons or human smuggling or certain offences in which an accused is alleged to have choked, suffocated or strangled a complainant; (f) expand the reverse onus provision to any person charged with a serious offence involving violence and the use of a weapon who has been previously convicted, within 10 years, of a serious offence involving violence and the use of a weapon; (g) add the number or gravity of any outstanding charges against an accused as circumstances that a justice is to consider in assessing whether the detention of the accused is necessary to maintain confidence in the adminis
b:C-14.sponsor: Sean Fraser (Liberal MP for Central Nova)
b:C-14.note: Amends the Criminal Code and related Acts on bail and sentencing, including reverse onus for certain violent, weapons and motor vehicle theft offences and conditions for release.

b:S-4.summary: This enactment amends the Energy Efficiency Act to, among other things, (a) enable the Minister of Natural Resources to provide for exemptions from the application of that Act and its regulations with the aim of facilitating the design and efficient administration of a regulatory regime to encourage innovation, competitiveness and economic growth; (b) strengthen that Act’s administration and enforcement framework, including by providing for administrative monetary penalties, modernizing fines and providing the Minister with the power to order corrective measures; and (c) broaden the scope of that Act to account for modern technologies and new market actors, address misleading representations and promote the responsible use of energy. Available on the Senate of Canada website at the following address: www.sencanada.ca/en 1st Session, 45th Parliament, 3 - 4 Charles III, 2025 SENATE OF CANADA BILL S-4 An Act to amend the Energy Efficiency Act
b:S-4.note: Amends the Energy Efficiency Act to allow regulatory exemptions, add administrative monetary penalties and corrective orders, and cover new technologies and market actors.

b:C-227.summary: This enactment provides for the development of a national strategy on housing for young Canadians to ensure they have greater access to affordable and secure housing. It also provides for reporting requirements in respect of the strategy.
b:C-227.note: Provides for a national strategy on housing for young Canadians to improve access to affordable and secure housing, with reporting requirements.

b:C-242.summary: This enactment amends the Criminal Code in order to (a) replace the principle of restraint in section 493.‍1 of the Act with the principle of protection of the public; (b) add the protection of the public as a consideration in decisions on the release of an accused; (c) add several violent indictable offences to the list of reverse-onus offences in subsection 515(6) of the Act for the determination of judicial interim release; (d) create a list of major offences, composed of violent reverse-onus offences; (e) prevent those charged with a major offence from being released after arrest by a peace officer; (f) require that only a superior court judge may determine, on a reverse-onus basis, whether to permit the interim release of an accused if the accused was charged with a major offence while they were on release in respect of another major offence and if they were convicted of a major offence in the last ten years; (g) provide for the expiry of the interim release of an accused upon their conviction of an indictable offence while they await sentencing; (h) prohibit those who have been convicted of an indictable offence in the last ten years from being named as a surety; (i) require that a justice assessing judicial interim release consider whether or not an accused is a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident and, if not, whether they may attempt to leave the country; (j) make it a condition that those who are not Canadian citizens or permanent residents deposit their passports in order to be released whether by a peace officer after arrest or by a justice on judicial interim release; and (k) change the standard of assessment under paragraph 515(10)‍(b) of the Act of whether an accused, if released, will commit an offence or interfere with the administration of justice
b:C-242.note: Amends the Criminal Code to make public protection a key factor in bail, expands reverse-onus offences, restricts releases and sureties, and requires passport deposits for non-citizens.

b:C-205.summary: This enactment amends the National Housing Strategy Act to require that the National Housing Strategy include measures to prevent the removal of homeless encampments on federal land and to identify alternatives to encampments. It also seeks to ensure that Indigenous peoples are involved and supported in determining and developing housing programs that affect them, and that responses to homeless encampments respect their rights. Finally, it specifies information to be included in the triennial report respecting the effectiveness of the Strategy.
b:C-205.sponsor: Jenny Kwan (NDP MP for Vancouver East)
b:C-205.note: Requires the National Housing Strategy to prevent removal of homeless encampments on federal land and identify alternatives, with Indigenous involvement and expanded triennial reporting.
